title: Activating the Core: Delving into the Effects of the Abdominal Drawing-In Technique on Back Muscle Dynamics in Exercises for Individuals with Non-specific Low Back Pain
content: This study investigates the impact of the abdominal drawing-in maneuver (ADIM) on the electromyographic (EMG) activity of spinal stabilizing muscles in individuals with non-specific low back pain during three exercises: prone trunk extension, superman, and unstable superman exercises. The research involved 40 participants, mostly female, with an average age of 21.42±1.07 years and a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 20.65±2.08 kg/m2. It focused on measuring EMG activity in key spinal stabilizing muscles during exercises performed with and without ADIM. Findings showed a significant increase in EMG activity for the iliocostalis lumborum pars thoracis and longissimus thoracis muscles when exercises were performed with ADIM. The most considerable changes were observed during the unstable superman exercise, indicating ADIM's potential to enhance the effectiveness of spinal stabilization exercises. The study confirms ADIM's role in modulating muscle activity, thereby supporting its inclusion in exercise routines for spinal alignment improvement and low back pain alleviation. However, it acknowledges the limitation of participants' unfamiliarity with ADIM and suggests future research include individuals of varying experience levels to verify the findings' generalizability.This study investigates the impact of the abdominal drawing-in maneuver (ADIM) on the electromyographic (EMG) activity of spinal stabilizing muscles in individuals with non-specific low back pain during three exercises: prone trunk extension, superman, and unstable superman exercises.
